subject: Planned: EastUS3 staggered kernel-module refresh — action items & fallback plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.ai>, Acme AI Ops <ops@acme.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Planned: EastUS3 staggered kernel-module refresh — action items & fallback plan

Hi Lena / Acme team,

Quick heads up: we’ve scheduled a staggered kernel-driver module refresh in the EastUS3 region to address a low-probability I/O edge case we observed under high-concurrency prefixes. Windows (UTC):

- Canary: 2028-04-17 22:00–23:00 UTC (5% capacity)
- Rollout group A: 2028-04-18 00:00–04:00 UTC
- Rollout group B: 2028-04-18 04:00–08:00 UTC

What to expect (customer-facing):
- Brief per-node kernel module reload and service process handoff; individual GPU-serving processes may restart and reconnect — typical interruption: ~30–90s for a single replica as KV caches warm.
- Automatic routing to compatible model variants during per-node restarts to maintain inference success; customers may see slightly increased tail latency for a small fraction of requests.
- Embeddings endpoints: expected to be unaffected for the majority of traffic; we will list exceptions below.

Action items for customers:
1) Confirm a primary on-call email/phone for the maintenance window so we can call out any critical anomalies.
2) If you want us to pre-warm caches for your tenancy (recommended for latency-sensitive flows), reply with tenant IDs by EOD 2028-04-13.
3) If you require a maintenance blackout, tell us by 2028-04-13 and we’ll propose an alternate window (may delay the patch).

We’ve attached the operator runbook and a short customer-impact matrix. Fallbacks: automatic routing to the most compatible model variant is configured; in the unlikely event of widespread errors we will fail over traffic to other regions or Dedicated capacity per your account settings.

Attachment highlights: eastus3-kmodule-runbook.pdf (operator steps), customer-impact-matrix.csv (per-endpoint expected behavior).

Thanks — we’ll do a brief pre-run internal canary and post-canary check before wide rollout.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Program Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0131

Subject: Re: Planned: EastUS3 staggered kernel-module refresh — action items & fallback plan

Thanks for the heads up, Neha — appreciate the detail. A couple quick questions: 

1) SLA credits: in case we see sustained errors during the window, what’s the exact process/lead time to request & get a credit?
2) Embeddings: you mentioned they’re expected to be unaffected — can you confirm whether high-concurrency batch embedding jobs (our async ingestion pipeline) might experience retries?
3) If we opt for pre-warm, are there any limits you need from us (tenant IDs, expected QPS windows)?

Lena Park
Head of Integrations, Acme AI
lena.park@acme.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned: EastUS3 staggered kernel-module refresh — technical notes

Neha / Monica — technical notes to include in customer reply: 

- Target module: nvidia-kmod-xg-4.1.2 (forward-compatible bugfix); reload is per-host and requires service process restart to pick up the new kernel module.
- Expected per-replica disruption: median ~45s, 95th ~75s during reconnect and KV cache rehydration.
- Embeddings (batch): async ingestion jobs that use large-batch embeddings may see transient retries if the worker action routes to a node that is restarting; recommend customers run with idempotent retries.
- Canary plan: apply patch to a small set of hosts 24 hours before full rollout and monitor error rates + 99th latency for 30m. If canary passes, proceed with Rollout group A.
- Mitigations in runbook: sticky routing to warm replicas, automated pre-warm when customers opt-in, and fall back to Dedicated or cross-region routing for critical SLAs.

Attachments: eastus3-kmodule-runbook.pdf (operator steps), also adding the quick-check checklist to the runbook for customer visibility.

Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.inference.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Planned: EastUS3 staggered kernel-module refresh — action items & fallback plan

Hi Lena — quick answers inline below.

1) SLA credits: if you see sustained errors above your configured thresholds (as captured in our console alerts) open a support ticket referencing SUP-98942 and our Billing team will evaluate credits. Typical acknowledgement timeline: 2–4 business hours after ticket with logs attached; resolution within 5 business days.

2) Embeddings/batch jobs: large-batch async ingestion jobs can see transient retry behavior if they hit a worker during a restart. We will not throttle ingestion jobs proactively; recommended option is to opt-in to pre-warm for your tenant (we will pin warm replicas ahead of the rollout). Please send tenant IDs and expected QPS by 2028-04-13 to opt in.

3) Pre-warm: we need tenant IDs and a peak-QPS estimate. Pre-warm is limited to 2 pre-warm groups per region for capacity planning — tell us which tenants to prioritize.

Next steps: I’ll schedule a short pre-canary check-in on 2028-04-17 21:30 UTC for any final alignment.

Link: https://redwood.app/docs/runbooks/eastus3-kmodule-refresh (runbook & quick-check checklist)

Best,
Neha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@acme.ai>, Acme AI Ops <ops@acme.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-04-19T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: EastUS3 kernel-module refresh — completed & post-maintenance summary

Hi Lena / team,

We completed the scheduled EastUS3 kernel-module refresh on 2028-04-18 per the phased plan. Summary: 

- Status: Completed for all rollout groups. Canary succeeded; no automatic rollback required.
- Customer impact: brief reconnects observed during per-host restarts; charts show small latency bumps during each micro-window but no sustained error-rate spikes above your SLA thresholds.
- Incidents: two hosts in Rollout group B had slower KV cache rehydration (extra ~60–120s) due to increased cache size; we triggered our fast-recover path and rebalanced warm replicas — affected requests retried and returned successfully.
- Postmortem: short-form postmortem attached (postmortem-summary.pdf) — includes timeline, root cause analysis, and recommended follow-ups.

Open items / recommended customer actions:
- If you had requested pre-warm and we did it for your tenant, no action needed. If you did not, and you observed elevated tail latency, please let us know and we’ll prioritize you for the next pre-warm window.
- If you’d like a 1:1 review of the postmortem and specific request for SLA credit, reply to this thread and reference SUP-98942.

Thanks for working through this with us — we’ll keep the runbook and the customer-impact matrix updated with the caching lessons learned.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Program Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
